task.description: HARD GATE. This diff touches a tenant-data path (multi-schema provisioning, and specifically a Repo.query call that interpolates a schema-name identifier into a CREATE SCHEMA statement, since Postgres cannot parameterize DDL identifiers). Review git diff main...HEAD on branch feature/WF02-REQ022-20260816 against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md, especially INV-7 (no string interpolation of tenant/user input into raw SQL). Pay particular attention to how schema_name is derived/constrained before it ever reaches the interpolated CREATE SCHEMA statement -- verify the constraint is real and actually enforced in code, not just claimed.
acceptance_criteria: no unsafe string interpolation of tenant/user-controlled input into raw SQL reaches the DB

the CREATE SCHEMA identifier-interpolation path is proven safe by an actual, enforced constraint on schema_name's shape (e.g. derived only from a UUID, never from free-text tenant input), not by assertion alone

result.summary: Scope test: YES (this diff IS the tenant-isolation mechanism -- new tenant_schemas table, provision_tenant_schema/1 issuing CREATE SCHEMA, replay_migrations/2). Full review run. INV-1 (tenant data isolation): APPLIES (decision 0003 is 'decided' -- schema-per-tenant via :prefix, per docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md -- and this is an S2 migration, so INV-1 is now checkable, not deferred). PASS: the one new table (tenant_schemas, priv/repo/migrations/20260816090045_create_tenant_schemas.exs) is structurally global like `tenants` itself (must be queryable before any tenant schema is known) and is correctly created unprefixed; no per-tenant business-data Ecto schema is added by this diff; tenant_scoped_migrations/0 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:198-200) is intentionally empty so no business table is yet placed behind a tenant schema by this change; the actual scoping mechanism decision B requires (Ecto :prefix) is correctly wired in replay_migrations/2 (tenant_provisioning.ex:160-177) via Ecto.Migrator.run(Repo, migration_source, :up, prefix: schema_name, ...). INV-2 (server-side field auth): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no API response-shaping code in this diff, S4 not started. INV-3 (sandboxing): NOT-APPLICABLE -- S5 not started, no scripting/plugin code. INV-4 (secrets by reference only): NOT-APPLICABLE -- diff adds/modifies no secret-resolving code. Ran both heuristic greps repo-wide anyway: `grep -rn System.get_env config/ lib/` = no matches; hardcoded-secret-literal heuristic = no matches. handoffs/orchestrator.log's new line references QUEUE_AUTH_TOKEN by name only (env var name, not its value) -- consistent with 'secrets by reference only'. INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no lookup-by-ID HTTP endpoint, S4 not started. INV-6 (new data-access paths prove scoping): APPLIES -- satisfied by this handoff itself (explicit per-invariant determination + verification evidence, status PASS). INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- the primary review target: APPLIES. PASS, verified by tracing schema_name's origin end to end, not by assertion. provision_tenant_schema/1 (tenant_provisioning.ex:99-137) accepts ONLY tenant_id -- grepped the whole repo for callers of provision_tenant_schema/schema_name_for_tenant/replay_migrations and found none outside tenant_provisioning.ex itself (no controller/route/external caller exists yet); there is no code path anywhere that lets an external caller supply a raw schema-name string. schema_name is derived exclusively by schema_name_for_tenant/1 (tenant_provisioning.ex:73-78): `Ecto.UUID.cast(tenant_id)` -> `{:ok, canonical} -> "tenant_" <> String.replace(canonical, "-", "")`. Read deps/ecto/lib/ecto/uuid.ex directly (not the design doc's claim): Ecto.UUID.cast/1 has exactly 3 clauses -- (1) a fixed-arity binary pattern match requiring exactly 36 bytes with literal `-` at byte offsets 9/14/19/24 and every other byte routed through a private `c/1` mapper that pattern-matches only 0-9/A-F/a-f and `throw(:error)` on anything else (catchable, forces the whole cast to return :error for non-hex/wrong-length/wrong-shape input, including any input containing a `"`, `;`, whitespace, or non-ASCII byte); (2) a raw 16-byte binary re-encoded via encode/1, which emits only via the `e/1` mapper (0-15 -> '0'-'9'/'a'-'f'), so this path also can only ever produce a canonical hex/hyphen string; (3) catch-all `cast(_), do: :error` for anything else (wrong type, wrong length). Both success paths are structurally incapable of producing a canonical string containing anything but lowercase hex digits and hyphens at fixed positions -- there is no way for attacker input to survive cast/1 with an embedded quote, semicolon, or space. After String.replace/3 strips the 4 hyphens, the result is exactly 32 lowercase hex chars; prepended with the literal "tenant_", the final schema_name provably matches ^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$ (39 chars, well under Postgres's 63-byte NAMEDATALEN limit -- no truncation-collision risk either). provision_tenant_schema/1 short-circuits on {:error, :invalid_tenant_id} (tenant_provisioning.ex:100-102) before ever reaching the interpolation, so a cast failure never reaches CREATE SCHEMA. The single interpolation site, `Repo.query!(~s(CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "#{schema_name}"))` (tenant_provisioning.ex:123), is therefore proven safe by an enforced constraint on schema_name's shape, not by comment/assertion alone. The companion advisory-lock query on the same line range correctly uses a real bind parameter (`Repo.query!("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1))", [schema_name])`, tenant_provisioning.ex:109) -- no unnecessary interpolation elsewhere. grep -rn Repo.query lib/ priv/repo/migrations/ found exactly these 2 hits, both manually confirmed safe (1 parameterized, 1 provably-constrained identifier); zero hits in priv/repo/migrations/ (declarative Ecto.Migration DSL only). Registration.changeset/2 (registration.ex) is a plain Ecto changeset feeding a normal Repo.insert (inherently parameterized regardless of field content) and is only ever called internally from provision_tenant_schema/1's insert_or_fetch_registration/2 with the already-derived, already-safe schema_name -- no external caller invokes it in this diff. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLIES. PASS. replay_migrations/2 explicitly wraps Ecto.Migrator.run/4 in try/rescue, converting any raised exception to the typed {:error, {:migration_failed, exception}} (tenant_provisioning.ex:169-176), matching the project's {:ok,_}|{:error,_} convention. provision_tenant_schema/1's two Repo.query! (bang) calls are unguarded, but this is the established, idiomatic 'let it crash' pattern INV-8's own text carves out (not a bare pattern match on realistic tenant input -- tenant_id is already validated via UUID cast before either bang call runs, and CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS with a provably-safe, already-existence-checked-via-advisory-lock identifier fails only for genuine infra reasons, e.g. permissions/connectivity). No caller of provision_tenant_schema/1 exists yet in this codebase (confirmed via repo-wide grep), so there is no evidence this runs inside a shared, long-lived, multi-tenant process today -- it is a stateless context-module function, matching Phoenix's per-request-process crash-isolation model, the same 'restart clean' case the invariant explicitly says is fine. Ran the INV-8 heuristic grep (`grep -rn '^\s*{:ok, .*} = ' lib/letflow/`); its 3 hits (identity.ex:171, tenant_provisioning.ex:126, tenant_provisioning.ex:214) are all false positives -- each is a `case` clause pattern match (`{:ok, %Struct{...} = x} ->`), not a bare crash-prone assignment; both new hits in tenant_provisioning.ex deliberately mirror the pre-existing, already-reviewed idiom in Letflow.Identity.insert_or_fetch/3 per the code's own comment. No genuine unguarded bare-match found.
